title: ALMA observations of water deuteration: a physical diagnostic of the formation of protostars
question: What is the HDO/H2O ratio in the inner warm gas of three isolated Class 0 protostars, and does it differ from clustered protostars?

what.value: HDO/H2O ratios of clustered protostars and comets for comparison

evidence.quote: assuming the Galactic oxygen isotope ratio of $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O$= 560$ (cite: wilson1994)

recipe.method: Pipeline calibration, phase self-cal, uvcontsub, tclean
Spectra at continuum peak after beam-matching; Gaussian fits (two for L483); CH3OCH3 blend subtracted for BHR71
Optically thin LTE, Tex=124 K; H2O from H2 18O with 16O/18O=560; HDO weighted average of two lines

evidence.quote: The estimated HDO/H$_2$O ratios for L483, B335, and BHR71–IRS1 are ($2.2\pm0.4$)$\times 10^{-3}$, ($1.7\pm0.3$)$\times 10^{-3}$, and ($1.8\pm0.4$)$\times 10^{-3}$
The excitation temperatures are 127$\pm24$ K, 174$\pm59$ K, and 103$\pm$21 K for L483, B335, and BHR71–IRS1

not_stated_but_needed: Image size, cell size, masking, deconvolution threshold
Integration windows and spectral extraction aperture details
HDO/H2 18O partition functions and spectroscopic constants used
score_reason: Public data and simple LTE recipe, but imaging and extraction details are sparse.
rediscovery_reason: Data public, simple LTE analysis, numeric ratios to compare.
